detailed_summary: This paper constructs short triorthogonal codes for qudits of odd prime dimension by generalizing the doubling construction, which combines a triorthogonal code with a code admitting a transversal phase gate, increasing the distance by up to two. The authors produce several new codes with parameters [[28,1,4]]_3, [[37,1,5]]_3, [[72,1,6]]_3, [[118,1,8]]_3, [[33,1,5]]_5, and [[20,1,4]]_7, each shorter than the best previously known cyclic, concatenated, and Reed-Muller codes of the same distance. They also give a doubling construction of the [[15,1,3]]_3 code. A key conceptual contribution is the interpretation of triorthogonality as the vanishing of multipole moments up to octupole order when columns of a generator matrix are viewed as charged points; doubling then corresponds to a double layer of opposite charges. This picture explains why inputs with nontrivial coefficients can yield shorter codes. Additionally, exhaustive search shows that the shortest distance-three codes have length 11 for p=5 and length 7 for p=7. Combined with high-rate distance-two codes, the new codes reduce the cost of qutrit magic state distillation by up to an order of magnitude in high-noise regimes.
key_contributions: Generalization of the doubling construction to qudits of odd prime dimension, yielding shorter triorthogonal codes with parameters [[28,1,4]]_3, [[37,1,5]]_3, [[72,1,6]]_3, [[118,1,8]]_3, [[33,1,5]]_5, and [[20,1,4]]_7.

A novel physical interpretation of triorthogonality as vanishing multipole moments (up to octupole) of charged points, with doubling as a double layer of opposite charges, providing intuition for why nontrivial coefficients can reduce code length.
Exhaustive search establishing the shortest distance-three codes for p=5 (length 11) and p=7 (length 7).
Demonstration that the new codes, when combined with high-rate distance-two codes, reduce the cost of qutrit magic state distillation by up to an order of magnitude in high-noise regimes.
A doubling construction of the [[15,1,3]]_3 code, showing the versatility of the method.
methodology_analysis: The authors generalize the doubling construction from qubits to qudits of odd prime dimension. Doubling combines a triorthogonal code with a code that admits a transversal phase gate, effectively increasing the distance by up to two while keeping the length short. The construction is algebraic, relying on properties of triorthogonal matrices over finite fields. The multipole moment interpretation is used as a guiding principle: columns of the generator matrix are treated as charged points in a d-dimensional space, and triorthogonality conditions correspond to the vanishing of moments up to octupole order. This allows the authors to design codes by arranging charges in layers of opposite sign, which cancels moments and leads to shorter codes. They also perform exhaustive searches for small distances to establish optimal lengths for p=5 and p=7. The methodology is primarily constructive and combinatorial, with theoretical justification provided by the moment interpretation.
results_analysis: The paper reports several new triorthogonal codes that are shorter than existing cyclic, concatenated, and Reed-Muller codes for the same distance. For example, the [[28,1,4]]_3 code improves on previous constructions, and the [[118,1,8]]_3 code is notably short for distance 8. The exhaustive search results show that the shortest distance-three codes have length 11 for p=5 and length 7 for p=7, which are likely optimal. The application to magic state distillation is quantified: the new codes reduce the cost by up to an order of magnitude in high-noise regimes, which is significant for fault-tolerant quantum computing with qutrits. The doubling of the [[15,1,3]]_3 code demonstrates the method's applicability to known codes.
strengths: Provides a clear and intuitive geometric interpretation (multipole moments) that explains the effectiveness of the doubling construction and guides the search for short codes.
Delivers concrete, improved code parameters that are shorter than previous best-known codes, with potential for significant practical impact in magic state distillation.
Includes exhaustive search results that establish optimality for small distances, adding rigor to the findings.
The construction is general for odd prime dimensions, making it widely applicable to qudit-based quantum computing.
limitations: The paper focuses on odd prime dimensions; extension to prime power dimensions or even dimensions is not addressed.
The practical implementation of the codes in magic state distillation is only briefly discussed; detailed resource overhead analysis and comparison with other distillation protocols are limited.
The exhaustive search is limited to distance three and small primes; optimality for higher distances or larger primes remains open.
connections_to_research: This work is directly relevant to quantum physics, particularly quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing with qudits. The construction of short triorthogonal codes is essential for efficient magic state distillation, a key component of universal quantum computation. The multipole moment interpretation connects to geometric and algebraic approaches in quantum coding theory, which may inspire further research in quantum information theory. The results also contribute to the broader understanding of qudit-based quantum error correction, which is an active area of interest in quantum physics.
overall_assessment: The paper presents a significant advance in quantum error correction for qudits by generalizing the doubling construction and providing a novel geometric interpretation. The new codes are shorter than previous best-known codes, and the application to magic state distillation shows practical relevance. The exhaustive search results add rigor. The work is novel, well-motivated, and of high quality, though it is somewhat specialized. It is likely to be of interest to researchers in quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.
